findings.claim: The allowlist parser only sees instructions spelled in uppercase at column 0, so the exact hazard the repair exists to catch — the whole context, `.git` included, copied into the published image — is GREEN when written `copy . /app/`, `Copy . /app/`, `add . /app/`, or with leading whitespace; and the same spellings in the derive stage falsely REDDEN a correct Dockerfile.
findings.evidence: src/browser/eval_adapter.py:6059 `re.finditer(r"(?m)^(?:COPY|ADD)\s+([^\n]*)$", text)` — case-sensitive literals anchored to column 0. Docker instruction keywords are case-insensitive and leading whitespace before an instruction is legal, so a line the parser does not match contributes no source and cannot be unlisted: the allowlist is default-red only for lines it parses, and default-GREEN for lines it does not. This is the fail-open-and-fail-closed-at-once signature the resolution artifact itself cites as the reason the denylist was retired. The diff also ships absolute prose that this falsifies: "survives Docker syntax nobody here has seen" and "no escape hatch" (case JSON ceiling (6), source comment, resolution artifact).

findings.acceptance: The shared instruction parser matches case-insensitively and tolerates leading whitespace (e.g. `(?mi)^[ \t]*(?:COPY|ADD)\s+`), watched red first with `copy . /app/` and an indented `COPY . /app/` added as self-test rows; or ceiling (4) is widened to name case and leading whitespace verbatim AND the absolute wording in ceiling (6), the source comment and the resolution artifact is struck. One regex fixes both directions, because both conjuncts read the same parser.
